A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Many-for-Many (MfM) research. All 31 pages, including equations, Tables 1-8, Figures 1-18 and Appendices A-H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation and manipulation experiments in Section 4, a multi-task training ablation, and an I2V user study in Appendix D and Table 8.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, training ablation, qualitative outputs and I2V user-study outcomes reported in v2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same conditional adapter, depth inputs, 3D-attention transformer, flow-matching objective and progressive joint image-video/multi-task training. The 2B and 8B architectures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources, including InsViE-1M, and retain VBench-T2V/I2V, the 16-task MfM-Benchmark and the I2V user-study scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in Tables 4-6 and 8 and the qualitative appendices. For example, inpainting still compares against VACE and ProPainter, while colorization compares against Colormnet and TCVC.

E3.justification: Training schedules, preprocessing and evaluation metrics are retained. Both specify 480 benchmark samples, 50 diffusion steps, guidance scale 9.0, and an I2V user study with 10 participants and 10 cases.

E4.justification: The multi-task versus single-task ablation in Section 4.4, Table 7 and Appendix F is unchanged. The qualitative comparisons and failure analyses in Appendices B, C, E and G also retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate and user-vote reporting practices. Neither introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match. MfM's average ranks remain 3.04 and 3.33 in Tables 4-5; Table 7 retains dynamic-degree scores of 0.819 versus 0.402; Table 8 retains 64.29% Top-1 and 85.71% Top-3 rates.

T1.justification: The adapter dimensional mapping and flow interpolation, velocity and loss expressions in Section 3, including Equations 1-2, are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified generation/manipulation, benefits from joint training, reduced training-data requirements and competitive performance with smaller models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning cross-task transfer and motion quality are unchanged. Both retain the multimodal-fusion limitation and Appendix G's failures involving physical interactions, rendered text and rapid motion, alongside the same broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: Architecture parameters, training recipes, processing instructions and benchmark-construction details match in Tables 2-3, Section 4.1 and Appendix A. Model, source-code and demonstration access links also remain the same.

R1.justification: The same 65 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning of MfM's joint training from scratch relative to VACE and specialized video models.

P1.justification: v3 places Ruibin Li before Tao Yang and removes Yuqi Zhang, Qide Dong and Haoran Cheng from the author list. The version/date stamp changes; body wording, section organization and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: The shorter author list is rearranged within the title-page byline, with small typesetting differences elsewhere. All figures and tables retain their designs, captions, panel arrangements and locations; appendix pages 15-31 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 retains the same methods, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. The author-list and minor typesetting changes do not materially improve or diminish the paper's scientific support or clarity.
